title: Solve FBM gap equation for Tc(p) with O-16 and O-18
action: Implement the FBM pairing propagator and linearized gap equation. For a set of doping points covering underdoped to overdoped, solve for Tc using a fast Fourier transform method (or equivalent iterative solver) for oxygen-16 and oxygen-18 masses. Store the resulting Tc arrays for the next step.
description: This process step computes the raw Tc values as a function of doping for both oxygen isotope masses. The arrays are used to derive the isotope shift in the next step.
output_schema: Internal arrays of Tc(K) for O-16 and O-18 as function of doping.

title: Compute isotope shift and output Tc(p) and alpha(p)
action: Using the Tc arrays from step1, compute the isotope shift exponent alpha(p) = -d ln Tc / d ln M (via finite difference). Write a CSV file with columns: doping_p, Tc_K, isotope_shift_alpha. The Tc values are for O-16.
description: Scored output: doping dependence of Tc and oxygen isotope shift alpha. Must show a hump in Tc and a dip in alpha near optimal doping.
output_schema: columns: doping_p (float), Tc_K (float), isotope_shift_alpha (float); rows for a representative set of dopings (e.g., 10-15 points).

title: Calculate dCDW gap and output chi_Q
action: Using the FBM parameters with K=0.23 eV, minimize the free energy of the one-dimensional d-wave CDW state to obtain the amplitude chi_Q. Write chi_Q in meV to a text file.
description: Scored output: dCDW gap magnitude chi_Q in meV.
output_schema: Single float (line) representing chi_Q in meV.

title: Output vibrational amplitude ratio
action: From the computed chi_Q (in eV) and the model parameters (n=3, n_s=2, K=0.23 eV, omega_a=0.05 eV), calculate the vibrational amplitude ratio sqrt(<u^2>)/sqrt(<x^2>) using the explicit formula: ratio = sqrt(2 * n_s * chi_Q^2 / (n * K * omega_a)). Write the ratio to a text file.
description: Second scalar output from the dCDW calculation.
output_schema: Single float (line) representing the ratio sqrt(<u^2>)/sqrt(<x^2>).
